findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption. Sensitive report data would be stored unencrypted at the bucket-policy level.
No ACL is set (defaulting behaviour) and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, leaving it without a guard against accidental public ACLs or bucket policies.
The bucket has no logging block, so object-level access to archived reports leaves no audit trail, hindering detection of unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be irrecoverably overwritten or deleted, including by an attacker attempting to destroy evidence.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, so a later policy or ACL change could expose ledger data publicly without a blocking control.
No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive ledger exports is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, allowing silent overwrite or deletion of ledger export objects with no recovery path.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted at rest by default.
No public access block is attached, so the bucket lacks defence-in-depth against accidental public exposure of model artifacts.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so operational runbooks (which frequently contain internal hostnames, procedures, and occasionally credentials) are stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or policies being applied later.
The runbooks bucket has no logging block, so reads of internal operational documentation are not auditable.
The audit log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so the security log repository is not protected against accidental public exposure by a future ACL or policy change.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket permits deletion of all audit logs along with the bucket, and no object lock or MFA delete is configured, weakening tamper-resistance of the audit trail.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing supplier PII/contact data) is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that itself has no default encryption, so the object is stored in cleartext.
